title: Measuring Validator Utility in Generate–Verify–Repair NetOps Pipelines: a Confirmatory Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (AC-2026-03) that measured whether a multidimensional validator-metric suite predicts end-to-end agentic NetOps success better than a single verifier pass rate. Using a synthetic intent→configuration generator and a hosted generate–validate–repair (GVR) adapter under shared_initial_candidate semantics, we ran 200 paired tasks (one shared initial generation per task reused for baseline and guarded). The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, v5.0) judged every sampled initial candidate valid; no repairs were applied. Baseline = 200/200, guarded = 200/200, paired difference = 0.00 (bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.00], exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10000). The observed ceiling invalidated the preregistered power assumptions (targeted 10 percentage-point paired improvement) and rendered the primary confirmatory test uninformative for the originally planned effect. We report preregistered design choices, precise execution accounting, representative validator-trace excerpts, quantitative analysis, artifact-grounded failure diagnostics, and reproducible prescriptions for follow-up preregistered experiments (fault injection, multi-sample generation, multi-validator comparison) required to estimate validator coverage and repair value.

sections.introduction:
Automating network operations (NetOps) with generative models offers promise for efficiency and scale, but operational deployment requires reliable mechanisms to avoid harmful or silently incorrect changes. A common operational pattern is generate–verify–repair (GVR): an LLM proposes a candidate configuration, a deterministic validator mechanically checks correctness and policy constraints, and, if needed, a repair module synthesizes corrections or escalates to human review. Prior system and benchmark work motivates verifier insertion, yet standardized, preregistered measurements of validator coverage (false-positive and false-negative rates), detection latency, and predictive usefulness for guarded end-to-end success remain underdeveloped.

This study (preregistered as AC-2026-03) asked: Can a standardized, empirically estimable validator metric suite (coverage, FP-rate, FN-rate, mean detection latency, operational-impact proxy) predict end-to-end agentic NetOps success better than a single raw verifier pass rate? We implemented a confirmatory paired design under shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each task the generator produced exactly one initial candidate that was reused by both baseline (no repair) and guarded (validator+repair permitted) conditions. Under these semantics any paired difference can arise only from downstream validator-triggered repair, not from independent generator sampling. Our contribution is (1) a fully preregistered, artifact-archived execution and analysis that reports a degenerate ceiling outcome, (2) diagnostic interpretation grounded in archived traces and configuration counts, and (3) concrete artifact-grounded prescriptions for follow-up preregistered experiments that can produce estimable validator FP/FN and repair utility.
sections.related_work:
Generate–verify–repair and closed-loop verifier architectures have been proposed and evaluated in code and system domains to reduce stochastic generator error and to enforce deterministic acceptance criteria [1]. Recent NetOps and AIOps benchmark efforts document substantive failure modes—ticket noise, false premises, and wrong-but-plausible outputs—that complicate end-to-end automation and motivate verifier layers [2],[3]. Prototype reports propose self-healing orchestrators, auditable decision traces, and verifier-guided repair to reduce silent or action-triggering failures in tool-augmented LLM systems [4]. Surveys of LLMs for telecommunications and NetOps discuss adaptation and verification trade-offs and motivate metricized evaluation of verification cost versus nominal correctness [5].

These works collectively motivate measurement of validator soundness and operational impact but do not deliver a standardized, empirically estimable validator-metric suite tailored to NetOps GVR flows. Our study intentionally treats prior demonstrations as architectural motivation and positions a preregistered measurement protocol and artifacts as a reproducible foundation for controlled follow-up experiments.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimands. The study was preregistered (AC-2026-03). The execution contract specified a paired binary design (conditions = [baseline, guarded]) with generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1, maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1, independent_condition_generation = false, and task_count = 200 pairs (planned_episode_count = 400). The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistered confirmatory test was a two-sided exact McNemar test with paired bootstrap-percentile 95% confidence intervals (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Power planning targeted detecting an absolute paired improvement of 0.10 (α = 0.05, ≈80% power) under conservative assumptions.

Task generation and constraints. Tasks were drawn deterministically from deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 (task_family = intent_configuration_repair_v1). Each task encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, a concise operator intent, allowed_fields and allowed_touched_fields, workflow policies (minimum_active_in_groups, must_be_down_for_fields), and a required_command_sequence that defines mechanistic checks. Task selection followed the preregistered deterministic challenging_workflow_stress_v1 index rule. Contamination controls (duplicate SHA exclusions and embedding-similarity exclusions with cosine > 0.95) were preregistered; none were triggered in this run (analysis/contamination_summary.csv empty).

Model and sampling. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json: declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini"). The adapter executed one shared initial generation per pair (provider-call audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 200). execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset). We explicitly state that temperature = null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted-model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; sampling nondeterminism may still be present at the provider side. The preregistration required recording runtime sampling parameters; those provider-call traces and audit fields are archived in the execution bundle.

Validator, scoring, and repairs. Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0). The validator implements mechanistic parsing and intent-constraint checks and emits per-episode fields: normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_codes, valid (boolean), repair_applied (boolean), and repair artifacts when invoked. The confirmatory binary success label used the preregistered scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation, i.e., validator.valid = true → success. The pipeline allowed at most one automated repair invocation per episode when validator.valid = false; repair traces would be recorded if executed.

Execution mechanics and missingness. The adapter was executed in scientific_confirmatory mode with maximum_attempts_per_call = 1 (no manual retries). The preregistered missingness plan used complete-pair analysis (primary) and a sensitivity scenario treating missing episodes as guarded failures. The execution manifest and analysis artifacts record completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, complete_pair_count = 200, and model_calls_used = 200.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The adapter completed the preregistered run: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 200, maximum_model_calls = 400. Provider-call audit (execution manifest) shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 200, and stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 200. No contamination or replacement exclusions occurred.

Primary confirmatory outcome. The deterministic validator judged every sampled shared initial candidate valid and applied no repairs. Summary statistics (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0), guarded successes = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0). Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n_11 = 200, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. The paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline = 0.00. Exact McNemar two-sided test p-value = 1.0. Bootstrap-percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.00, 0.00]. All reported numeric artifacts (condition summaries, contingency table, analysis log) are archived under analysis/ in the execution bundle.

Representative validator-trace excerpt. A compact exemplar from pair-000004 (verbatim relevant fields from execution/scoring/task-000004-guarded.json):

  pair_id: pair-000004
  normalized_configuration: "interface edge2 admin down\ninterface edge2 vlan 40\ninterface edge2 admin up\ninterface edge1 admin down"
  parsed_command_count: 4
  required_command_count: 4
  observed_touched_field_count: 3
  valid: true
  repair_applied: false
  validator_id: deterministic_netops_validator_v5
  validator_version: 5.0

For this exemplar the parsed and required command counts match, no violation codes were emitted, and the validator did not request repair. Equivalent validator_trace.validation_after.valid = true and repair_applied = false hold for every archived episode; hence repair-based differences could not occur under shared_initial_candidate semantics.

Exploratory diagnostics. Because repair_applied = false for all episodes, per-validator FP/FN and detection-latency distributions are degenerate and uninformative for the original estimand. The archived raw responses and validator traces (execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/scoring/*.json) permit reanalysis under alternative scoring rules or under injected-fault conditions described below.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of the degenerate outcome. The paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics isolates downstream validator-triggered repair effects by ensuring the baseline and guarded conditions evaluated the identical initial candidate per pair. This property is scientifically useful for attributing any paired improvement to subsequent repair, but it also concentrates the risk of a single-sample ceiling: if the generator (for the sampled seeds) and the validator align on correctness, no repairs are triggered and the paired estimator has zero variance. That is precisely the artifact-grounded outcome observed: every initial candidate satisfied the validator's mechanistic checks, producing a ceiling that invalidated the preregistered power assumptions (targeted 10% absolute paired improvement).

Why the ceiling occurred: three archived determinants. (1) The synthetic deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 encoded constrained, mechanistically checkable intents and reference sequences that the generator matched for the recorded generation seeds. (2) The single-sample-per-task sampling regime removed generator variability as a source of discordance between baseline and guarded. (3) The deterministic validator enforces mechanistic structural and policy checks but does not detect semantic intent misalignment beyond encoded rules (i.e., correct-by-structure but possibly incorrect-by-intent remains undetectable without additional semantic or operator feedback signals). The execution artifacts explicitly show these features (task payloads with required_command_sequences, single shared-initial response files, and validator_trace fields).

Artifact-grounded prescriptions for follow-up preregistered arms. To produce estimable validator FP/FN and repair utility while preserving preregistered rigor, the archived adapter and task generator already support three immediate, deterministic, preregisterable extensions:
  1) Fault-injection arm (preregistered): deterministically replace a fraction f of reference answers with injected faults (syntactic errors, configuration-logic faults, semantic-intent swaps) prior to generation or as a deterministic post-hoc modification of the generator outputs. This guarantees non-zero baseline invalidity and allows measurement of repair invocation rates and repair success.
  2) Multi-sample generation: set initial_generation_calls_per_task = k ≥ 3 independent draws per task and allow the guarded pipeline to accept any validator-approved candidate among draws or to invoke repair. Multiple independent samples reintroduce generator variance and create opportunities for validator rejection and repair.
  3) Multi-validator and multi-model comparison: add at least one alternative validator implementation and at least one additional model family. This quantifies sensitivity of measured FP/FN to validator design and model diversity and improves external validity beyond the single validator and model used here.
Each prescription is implementable deterministically using the archived manifests and the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter semantics; the execution bundle contains the manifest fields and provider-call auditing needed to reproduce and preregister these arms.

Threats to validity and operational implications. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally isolate repair effects but produce single-sample ceiling risk; future designs should preregister multi-sampling or injected-fault arms to avoid degeneracy. Construct validity: validator.valid operationalizes mechanistic correctness but does not capture semantic alignment with operator intent; an operational-impact proxy or human adjudication channel is required to measure semantic misalignment. External validity: our synthetic task bank, single model (gpt-5-mini), and single deterministic validator limit generalization to multi-vendor production networks. Conclusion validity: with zero variance in the primary estimand the confirmatory test provides a correct null result but no evidence about repair efficacy.

Practical takeaways. Deterministic validators remain essential for catching syntactic and policy violations; however, meaningful measurement of their coverage and repair value requires experimental designs that produce measurable baseline invalidity or sample generator variability. Preregistered fault-injection and multi-sample regimes are concrete, artifact-supported next steps to produce estimable FP/FN and repair-utility statistics.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory study (AC-2026-03) under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure validator utility in NetOps GVR pipelines. For the synthetic task bank, sampled gpt-5-mini seeds, and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 used here, every sampled initial candidate passed the validator's mechanistic checks so no repairs were applied and guarded success equaled baseline (200/200). The preregistered power assumptions were invalidated by this ceiling outcome. The result is artifact-grounded and reproducible from the archived bundle. We publish exact execution and analysis artifacts and provide concrete preregistered experiment prescriptions (fault injection, multi-sample generation, multi-validator comparison) required to produce non-degenerate, estimable validator FP/FN behavior and repair value in operationally meaningful conditions. The archived artifacts support direct replication and preregistered follow-up runs using the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter and deterministic task generator described herein.

limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics constrained inference: baseline and guarded reused the same initial candidate per pair; any paired difference could only arise from validator-triggered repair (not from independent generator sampling).
Synthetic task bank (difficulty 'very_hard'/'extreme') is not equivalent to heterogeneous production networks (multi-vendor devices, real ticket noise); external validity is limited.
Single-model experiment: only gpt-5-mini was executed; no multi-model generality claims are made.

No repairs were applied because all initial candidates passed the deterministic validator; therefore the study could not estimate repair effectiveness or validator false-negative behavior in this execution.

Validator scope: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces mechanistic intent-constraint checks but does not guarantee detection of semantic intent misalignment (correct-by-structure but incorrect-by-intent).
Recorded execution/model_configuration.json temperature = null/unset does not imply deterministic sampling; provider-side sampling behavior may vary and is documented in execution manifests.
